title: redirect()/revalidatePath() run inside the withTenantScope body at ~14 real call sites, and nothing states or enforces the invariant
why_open: withTenantScope is defined at apps/web/src/lib/tenant-scope.ts:409-418 and runs fn() inside runInTenantScope (apps/web/src/lib/tenancy/context.ts:84-89), whose settleInsideContext wraps the body in Promise.resolve so the whole body — including any db.$transaction it opens — settles inside the AsyncLocalStorage scope. Real call sites end the scope body with a Next.js control-flow throw: apps/web/src/app/(app)/admin/actions.ts:73 (redirect after chartClub), apps/web/src/app/(app)/messages/actions.ts:135, :190, :224, :255, :319, apps/web/src/app/(app)/calendar/actions.ts:166-168 (revalidatePath x2 then redirect), apps/web/src/app/(app)/orgs/[slug]/documents/actions.ts:113 and :214, apps/web/src/app/(app)/orgs/actions.ts:46,:102-104,:142-144,:159-161, apps/web/src/app/(app)/feed/actions.ts:51,:84,:154,:233, apps/web/src/app/(app)/actions.ts:45. Nothing anywhere asserts the invariant: tests/architecture/ has 15 static guards (forbidden-clients, guards-do-not-write-into-the-tree, nav-hrefs-are-served, ...) and tests/security/ has 28, and grep for NEXT_REDIRECT across apps, packages, tests and tools returns nothing. apps/web/src/lib/tenant-scope.test.ts and apps/web/src/lib/tenancy/context.test.ts never mention redirect. So the invariant REVIEW-FINDINGS.md:53 names is unwritten and unenforced, and the moment any of these bodies is refactored to wrap its writes in db.$transaction the write is silently rolled back while the browser follows the redirect.
smallest_real_change: Make the invariant executable in runInTenantScope, then fix every call site in the same change. (1) In apps/web/src/lib/tenancy/context.ts add isNavigationSignal(err) — an object whose `digest` is a string starting with "NEXT_REDIRECT" or equal to "NEXT_NOT_FOUND" — and have runInTenantScope catch it (both synchronously and on the returned promise, since settleInsideContext already owns the thenable) and rethrow a TenantContextError naming the signal and telling the author to return the target and navigate after the scope closes. (2) Rewrite each call site to `const target = await withTenantScope(userId, async () => { ...; return "/messages/" + convo.id })` followed by `redirect(target)`, and hoist every revalidatePath/revalidateTag out of the body the same way (collect the paths, return them, revalidate after). That is ~14 sites across the 7 action files listed; skip apps/web/src/app/(app)/approvals/actions.ts:181-182 and :500-505, which another run owns. (3) Add tests/architecture/navigation-outside-tenant-scope.test.mjs in the shape of tests/architecture/forbidden-clients.test.mjs (git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard over apps/web/src/app, comments stripped) failing when redirect(/revalidatePath(/revalidateTag( appears lexically inside a withTenantScope(/withSystemTenantScope(/forEachInstitution(/runInTenantScope( callback, with the approvals path listed as an explicitly-reasoned exemption owned elsewhere. MUTATION PROOF: move the redirect at apps/web/src/app/(app)/messages/actions.ts back inside the scope body — the static guard must red — and separately, in apps/web/src/lib/tenancy/context.test.ts, run a scope body that throws { digest: 'NEXT_REDIRECT;/x;307;' } and assert TenantContextError; delete the catch in context.ts and that test must red. Do not assert on a helper: the static guard reads the production action files, and the runtime test drives withTenantScope, not isNavigationSignal. DEDUPE: surveyors 1, 4 and 6 filed this same P1 (as WRK-P1-16-REDIRECT-OUTSIDE-TENANT-SCOPE, WRK-GATE-010 and REVIEW-FINDINGS-16-redirect-inside-withTenantScope) — the orchestrator asked every surveyor to carry it; implement it ONCE. SERIALISE: apps/web/src/lib/tenancy/context.ts is dirty in the working tree right now — a concurrent run has added a required `environment: PaymentMode` field to TenantScope (git diff apps/web/src/lib/tenancy/context.ts) while apps/web/src/lib/tenant-scope.ts, whose scopeForUser at :165-170 and withSystemTenantScope at :433-436 construct TenantScope, is NOT yet updated. Do not edit either file concurrently with that run, and re-read both before starting.

title: Nothing verifies an inbound provider event: no raw-body signature check, no replay window, no subscription verification or renewal — the receiving edge does not exist
why_open: WRK-060-002 is about events ARRIVING from a provider. There is no inbound event endpoint of any kind: `find apps/web/src/app/api -name route.ts` lists 22 routes and not one is a webhook (admin/directory, ai/chat, ai/draft, attachment, auth, calendar/event, calendar/ics, calendar/reschedule, documents, health, jobs/reminders, me, notifications, org-image, platform/export, platform/reconcile, profile-image, reports/pulse, search, templates/budget). Grep for webhook/Webhook across apps/web/src and packages/*/src returns only prose: apps/web/src/lib/tenant-scope.ts:423 and packages/configuration/src/configuration.test.ts:89. So there is no raw-body signature verification, no timestamp/nonce replay window, and no subscription (Graph change-notification / Google watch / Slack Events) verification or renewal anywhere. The only inbound-authentication precedent in the tree is a shared bearer secret compared over a hash — apps/web/src/app/api/platform/reconcile/route.ts:34-40,:59-62 — which authenticates the CALLER and says nothing about the BODY, and it reads `request.json()` (:66) so the raw bytes a signature must cover are already gone by the time anything could check them. COLLISION: a concurrent cluster run is building the OUTBOUND half (untracked migration apps/web/prisma/migrations/20260807143000_outbox_dispatch_and_inbox/ adds OutboxEvent.dispatchedAt/origin and an InboxEvent table for PAY-020-005/006, and apps/web/src/lib/outbox/outbox.ts is modified in the working tree). Surveyors 4 and 6 also filed the missing outbound runner as WRK-060-001 / WRK-060-003. This item is deliberately scoped to the INBOUND edge only — do not touch apps/web/src/lib/outbox/outbox.ts, and consume the InboxEvent table that run is adding rather than inventing a second one.
smallest_real_change: (1) apps/web/src/lib/http/webhook-signature.ts — the edge-safe half, no next/*, no @/lib/db, matching the discipline apps/web/src/lib/http/internal-headers.ts:47-49 already states: verifySignedDelivery({ rawBody, headers, secret, now, toleranceMs }) that recomputes an HMAC over the EXACT bytes (never over a re-serialised object), compares with timingSafeEqual over equal-length digests as apps/web/src/app/api/platform/reconcile/route.ts:34-40 does, refuses when the signed timestamp is outside the tolerance window, and refuses a delivery id already seen. Return a typed refusal (BAD_SIGNATURE / OUTSIDE_WINDOW / REPLAYED / UNKNOWN_PROVIDER), never a boolean, so the route can log which. (2) apps/web/src/app/api/connectors/[provider]/events/route.ts is the production caller: it reads `await request.text()` FIRST, resolves the provider through the capability registry (WRK-GATE-080) and 404s any provider not registered AVAILABLE — so with today's registry every provider 404s and the endpoint claims nothing — verifies, records the delivery id in the InboxEvent table the concurrent run is adding (that write is the replay defence, and it is what makes acceptance durable), and returns 202 without doing any provider work inline. MUTATION PROOF: drive the ROUTE, not the helper. Post a body whose signature was computed over a re-ordered JSON re-serialisation and assert 401 (this is the mutation that catches the classic bug of verifying over the parsed object); post the same signed delivery twice and assert 202 then 409-with-REPLAYED and exactly one InboxEvent row; post a delivery signed 10 minutes ago and assert OUTSIDE_WINDOW. Then mutate the producer — have the route call `request.json()` and re-stringify before verifying — and the first test must red. Subscription verification/renewal (Graph subscription expiry, Google watch renewal) has no provider to renew against yet and should be recorded as still FAIL rather than claimed.

title: Relay answers carry no freshness, no source-vs-inference distinction and no governed citation — the model is told to cite numbers over rows with no observation time
why_open: The Relay answer path is real and wired: apps/web/src/app/api/ai/chat/route.ts:99-108 authorizes the search.corpus tool then maps ranked docs to `sources` as { title, href, kind, context } only, and :133-137 instructs the model to 'Cite every claim with its source number in brackets'. The citation carries no observation time, no staleness verdict and no statement of whether the claim is a retrieved fact or an inference. SearchDoc itself has no such fields — apps/web/src/lib/search.ts:7-14 is { id, kind, title, body, href, context }, and apps/web/src/lib/search-data.ts:52-54 selects `id, title, content, roleId, organizationId` for memory records with no updatedAt at all. Grep for citation/freshness across apps/web/src and packages/*/src finds only packages/finops/src/reporting.ts:54-68 (a Freshness type for cost reporting, in a package another run owns) and the word 'citation' in a comment at apps/web/src/lib/search.ts:13. Bible §3.5 requires that a stale, deleted or inaccessible source is never answered as though current, and §9.3 requires governed provider deep-links; today neither exists on the one production path that cites anything.
smallest_real_change: Add the citation value and make the answer path unable to emit a source without one. (1) packages/work-graph/src/citation.ts: `SourceCitation` = { origin: 'TENURE_RECORD' | 'EXTERNAL_PROJECTION', assertion: 'SOURCE' | 'INFERENCE', observedAt: string, projectionState: 'CURRENT' | 'STALE' | 'SOURCE_DELETED' | 'ACCESS_REVOKED' | 'SOURCE_UNKNOWN', deepLink: string | null } with parseSourceCitation() and freshnessAt(observedAt, now, staleAfterMs) implementing the §3.5 ladder, plus governedDeepLink(providerId, url) that returns null unless the provider is registered AVAILABLE and the URL's origin matches that provider's declared host — never the raw stored URL. (2) Widen SearchDoc in apps/web/src/lib/search.ts with a required `citation: SourceCitation`; the ONLY construction site is apps/web/src/lib/search-data.ts:84 (plus the fixture at apps/web/src/lib/search.test.ts:259), so add `updatedAt` to each of the four selects there and build the citation per row — required, not optional, so a caller that forgets is a compile error rather than an invisible runtime hole. (3) apps/web/src/app/api/ai/chat/route.ts:103-108 emits the citation with each source, and :133-137's sourceBlock prefixes each numbered source with its state and observedAt so the model cannot present a STALE row as current. MUTATION PROOF: assert on what the route EMITS — a test that drives POST with a corpus row whose updatedAt is older than the stale window and asserts both the returned source and the prompt text carry STALE; then mutate the producer (freeze projectionState to 'CURRENT' in search-data.ts) and it must red. A test that calls freshnessAt() directly proves nothing once the route stops calling it. NEIGHBOUR: surveyor 4's WRK-GATE-070 covers the same SearchDoc/chat-route area from the 'answers are not citation-verified' angle — give both to one agent, they are the same edit to apps/web/src/lib/search.ts, search-data.ts and api/ai/chat/route.ts.

title: None of the canonical Work Graph objects exist — no ExternalObjectRef, SourceCitation, SyncObservation, Tombstone or projection-state type anywhere in the tree
why_open: Bible §3.2 lists ~60 canonical objects and §3.5 a projection state machine (DISCOVERED -> AUTHORIZED -> FETCH_PENDING -> CURRENT -> STALE -> REFRESHING plus ten exceptional states). There is no work-graph package: `ls packages/` returns audit, authorization, configuration, contracts, finops, identity, metadata, module-runtime, organization-model, platform-config, provisioning, releases, workflow and nothing else. Grep for ExternalObjectRef / SyncObservation / Tombstone / IndexProjection / ConnectionGrant across apps and packages returns zero hits. The nearest thing, packages/identity/src/connection-lifecycle.ts:37-101, is an SSO/SAML federation connection (DRAFT/VALIDATED/TESTED/ACTIVE/DISABLED, signing keys, assertion tests) — a different concept in a different domain, and applyConnectionAction at :161 has no production caller either (only packages/identity/src/index.ts:295 re-exports it). Neither the objects nor the state machine exist.
smallest_real_change: Do not declare 60 types nobody calls — that is the dead-code failure this bar forbids. Ship the four the citation path (WRK-070-003) actually consumes, and let that path be the caller: ExternalObjectRef (tenant, providerId, productId, external workspace/account, objectType, opaque externalId, version/etag, created/modified/deleted, classification, connectorReleaseId, observedAt), SourceCitation, SyncObservation and Tombstone, each with a parse* function that refuses a value missing tenant/provider/externalId, plus projection-state.ts implementing the §3.5 transition table (advance(state, event) returning the next state or a refusal, with SOURCE_DELETED/ACCESS_REVOKED/RETENTION_EXPIRED terminal to CURRENT). Wire it by making apps/web/src/lib/search-data.ts build every Tenure row's citation through parseSourceCitation, so the parser is on the request path rather than beside it. MUTATION PROOF: assert through the /api/ai/chat response, not through the parser — remove `observedAt` from the row built in search-data.ts and the route test must red with the parser's refusal. Every remaining §3.2 object stays unwritten until a caller needs it, and the ledger entry says so rather than claiming 60 objects exist.

title: A Microsoft Graph two-way calendar sync is claimed in code and to users, with no connector, no certification and a process-global provider slot that ignores tenancy
why_open: apps/web/src/lib/calendar-sync.ts:10-12 states 'When Microsoft Graph credentials are provided, a real two-way GraphCalendarSync implements the CalendarSyncProvider below and drops in with no change to callers', and :83-84 of apps/web/src/components/CalendarSubscribe.tsx repeats it to the user: 'Two-way sync (edits made in Outlook flowing back into Tenure) turns on once your institution connects Microsoft 365.' No such connector exists — grep for Microsoft Graph / graph.microsoft.com across apps and packages returns nothing but those two claims. Worse, the seam they point at is dead: calendarSync() (apps/web/src/lib/calendar-sync.ts:29) and setCalendarSyncProvider() (:32) have zero callers anywhere in the tree, so the 'drops in with no change to callers' clause is true only because there are no callers. And the slot itself is a module-level mutable singleton (`let provider` at :28) with no tenant in its key: one institution's connector, once set, would serve every institution in the process — WRK-GATE-020's 'cannot exceed granted tenant authority' violated by construction, before any provider is ever written. There is no provider/product/capability status registry of any kind (WRK-000-002's PLANNED/DEVELOPMENT/CERTIFICATION_PENDING/AVAILABLE/DEGRADED/SUSPENDED/UNSUPPORTED vocabulary appears nowhere in code).
smallest_real_change: (1) Delete the uncalled CalendarSyncProvider interface, IcsFeedSync, the `let provider` singleton, calendarSync() and setCalendarSyncProvider() from apps/web/src/lib/calendar-sync.ts:15-34, and rewrite the module comment so it claims only what ships: a per-user ICS feed. Nothing imports them, so the deletion breaks no caller — confirm with grep before and after. (2) packages/work-graph/src/capability-status.ts holds the real registry: entries of { providerId, productId, capabilityKey, direction, status } over the seven WRK-000-002 statuses, seeded with `ics-feed / calendar / publish / OUTBOUND / AVAILABLE` and `microsoft-365 / calendar / two-way-sync / BIDIRECTIONAL / PLANNED`, plus capabilityIsOffered() which returns true only for AVAILABLE. Its production caller is apps/web/src/app/(app)/calendar/page.tsx:219, whose 'subscribe to keep Outlook in sync' copy becomes a lookup, so the sentence a user reads cannot outrun the registry. (3) tests/architecture/no-uncertified-provider-claims.test.mjs, in the shape of tests/architecture/forbidden-clients.test.mjs, scans apps/web/src/lib and apps/web/src/app for provider brand names bound to capability verbs (sync/send/create/two-way) and fails unless the file also reads the registry. NOTE FOR THE IMPLEMENTER: apps/web/src/components/CalendarSubscribe.tsx:83-84 carries the same false claim and apps/web/src/components is owned by another cluster run — do not edit it; scope the guard to lib/ and app/ and record the component line as an open follow-up owned elsewhere. WRK-110-001 (Connection Center surfaces) is FAIL for the same ownership reason: it is entirely apps/web/src/components. MUTATION PROOF: flip the microsoft-365 entry to AVAILABLE and the calendar page test asserting the rendered copy must change; flip it back. Then re-add a bare brand claim to calendar-sync.ts and the architecture guard must red.

title: No connection classes exist, so nothing can prohibit class escalation — a read grant and an org-wide app identity are indistinguishable
why_open: Bible §4.1 names eight classes (USER_DELEGATED, ADMIN_DELEGATED, APPLICATION_ORG_WIDE, BOT_OR_APP_INSTALLATION, SERVICE_ACCOUNT, WEBHOOK_ONLY, FILE_OR_FEED, PERSONAL_PRODUCTIVITY) and requires that connection class, provider consent and Tenure authorization all agree. Grep for USER_DELEGATED / APPLICATION_ORG_WIDE / WEBHOOK_ONLY / connection class across apps/web/src and packages/*/src returns nothing. The one authorization surface a connector would pass through is apps/web/src/lib/relay-tools.ts:81-126, and it decides on `tool.requiredPermission` alone — a ToolRegistration carries no connection class, no direction and no resource selector, so a tool declared by any module is offered on the strength of a Tenure permission with nothing representing what the provider actually consented to. There is no place in the codebase where the sentence 'this connection may not do that' can currently be written.
smallest_real_change: packages/work-graph/src/connection-class.ts declares the eight classes as a const tuple with, for each, the maximum action direction it may reach (READ / DRAFT / WRITE / ADMIN) and whether it may serve tenant-wide use (PERSONAL_PRODUCTIVITY may not). Export refuseEscalation(granted, requested) returning either { ok: true } or a refusal naming both classes — never a boolean, so the reason survives to the caller. Make it real at the one live decision point: extend the registry entry from WRK-GATE-080 with the connection class the capability is offered under, and have authorizeRelayTools in apps/web/src/lib/relay-tools.ts:101-123 refuse a tool whose required direction exceeds the class its capability is registered under, pushing a RefusedTool with that reason — which apps/web/src/app/api/ai/chat/route.ts:151-155 already surfaces as `toolRefusal`. MUTATION PROOF: register a probe capability at WEBHOOK_ONLY whose tool needs WRITE, POST /api/ai/chat and assert the response's toolRefusal names the escalation; then mutate the producer — make relay-tools.ts skip the class check — and the route test must red. Do not call refuseEscalation() from the test directly. CONSUMERS CHECKED: RelayToolset/OfferedTool/RefusedTool are consumed only by apps/web/src/app/api/ai/chat/route.ts:99-100,:151-155 and apps/web/src/app/api/ai/ai-kill-switch.test.ts:122; ToolRegistration itself lives in packages/contracts and must NOT be widened — another run owns it, which is why the class is carried on the capability registry entry instead.

title: viewerTimeZone is React.cache()d on userId alone and reads a tenant-scoped row, so the second tenant in a request gets the first tenant's answer
why_open: REVIEW-FINDINGS.md:54 states the invariant that no cache()d function may return tenant rows, and apps/web/src/lib/institution-time.ts:30-44 breaks it: viewerTimeZone = cache(async (userId) => ...) queries db.organization.findFirst (Organization is tenant-scoped — the tenancy extension filters it, apps/web/src/lib/tenancy/extension.ts:66-77) and its cache key contains no institution at all. It also resolves from ctx.institutionRoles[0] rather than the acting scope, so a two-institution user who switched tenants via chooseActingInstitution (apps/web/src/lib/tenant-scope.ts:294-327) is shown their FIRST institution's timezone on every calendar surface. React.cache is per-request, and a request can legitimately open two scopes, so the memoized value crosses a tenant boundary within one render. Production callers: apps/web/src/app/(app)/calendar/page.tsx:58, apps/web/src/app/(app)/calendar/new/page.tsx:39, apps/web/src/app/(app)/feed/page.tsx:41. Nothing asserts the invariant — tests/security/authority-is-not-cached.test.mjs covers module-level Maps in rbac/identity only, and grep for the invariant's wording across tests/ returns nothing.
smallest_real_change: Take the tenant from the open scope instead of from the user. Change viewerTimeZone to `cache(async (userId: string, institutionId: string) => ...)` and delegate straight to institutionTimeZone(institutionId) (already correctly keyed at apps/web/src/lib/institution-time.ts:17), keeping the orgRoles fallback only for a user with no membership in that institution; the three page callers already sit inside withTenantScope and pass `scope.institutionId`. That both fixes the wrong-timezone-after-switch bug and puts the tenant in the cache key. Then extend tests/security/authority-is-not-cached.test.mjs (or add a sibling) with a static check over apps/web/src/lib and apps/web/src/app: a `cache(` whose body reaches @/lib/db on a model the tenancy registry classifies tenant-scoped must take an institutionId parameter, with each exemption stating why. CONSUMERS CHECKED: viewerTimeZone has exactly three call sites (listed above) and institutionTimeZone has five (admin/overrides/page.tsx:30, calendar/actions.ts:48, calendar/[id]/page.tsx:39, calendar-write.ts:443,:632,:713) — the signature change is a compile error at all of them, which is the point. MUTATION PROOF: an itest against the running Postgres that puts one user in two institutions with different timeZone values, renders under scope A then scope B in one request, and asserts two different zones; revert viewerTimeZone to the userId-only key and it must red. DEDUPE: surveyor 1 filed the same defect as WRK-P1-16-CACHE-IS-PER-REQUEST-NOT-PER-SCOPE — implement it once. The signature change touches apps/web/src/lib/tenant-scope.ts's scope object only through `scope.institutionId`, which is stable, but that file is dirty in a concurrent run (see REVIEW-16-REDIRECT) — re-read before starting.

title: Strict egress does not exist — the ECS task security group allows all outbound to 0.0.0.0/0, which is the one control a connector cloud cannot do without
why_open: infrastructure/terraform/security_groups.tf:53-58 gives the ECS task security group `egress { from_port = 0, to_port = 0, protocol = "-1", cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"] }` with the comment 'Allow all outbound (ECR pull, RDS, Redis, SQS, SES, Secrets Manager)'; the ALB group at :30-35 is the same. There are no VPC interface endpoints in infrastructure/terraform (the .tf files are acm, alb, cloudfront, cloudwatch, dev-login-gate, ecr, ecs, edge-access, elasticache, main, outputs, rds, s3, scheduler, secrets, security_groups, ses, sqs, variables, vpc — no aws_vpc_endpoint). Nothing in tests/security asserts an egress boundary; tests/security/cell-independence.test.mjs is an import survey, not a network one. WRK-120-002 asks for 'strict egress' precisely because a connector runner holds provider tokens and tenant content: with a wildcard egress rule, a compromised dependency in the task can post either to any host on the internet, and no other control in this design would notice. Backup/DR is also short of the requirement — infrastructure/terraform/rds.tf:48 is `backup_retention_period = 1` with a comment deferring the raise, and there is no per-tenant restore runbook anywhere under docs/.
smallest_real_change: Replace the wildcard with a stated boundary. (1) infrastructure/terraform/endpoints.tf: an S3 gateway endpoint plus interface endpoints for ecr.api, ecr.dkr, secretsmanager, sqs, logs and email-smtp, each with a security group that accepts 443 from the ECS group. (2) In security_groups.tf, narrow the ECS egress to 443 towards those endpoint security groups and the RDS/Redis groups, and add ONE explicitly-reasoned egress rule per certified provider host (none today — the AVAILABLE set from WRK-GATE-080 is ics-feed only, which is inbound, so the provider list starts empty and every future connector has to add its own rule and say why). (3) tests/security/egress-is-bounded.test.mjs parses the .tf files and fails on any egress block on the ECS or RDS group carrying cidr_blocks 0.0.0.0/0 or protocol "-1", with an allowlist whose every entry states a reason — the shape tests/architecture/forbidden-clients.test.mjs already uses. Verify with `terraform validate` and `terraform plan` only; DO NOT apply, and do not touch the `if: github.repository == 'Tenurework/Tenure'` guards in .github/workflows. MUTATION PROOF: re-add the wildcard egress to the ECS group and the new test must red; remove it and it passes. HONEST SCOPE: this closes 'strict egress' for WRK-120-002. Cell/region isolation, least IAM, backup/restore and DR are separate and remain FAIL — rds.tf:48 keeps retention at 1 day on the free tier, which is a BLOCKED_EXTERNAL on the AWS account plan, and that should be recorded as such rather than passed.

title: The command bus that would carry action risk, plan digest, reauthorization and receipt has no production caller, and wiring it needs a Prisma model another run owns
why_open: apps/web/src/lib/commands/bus.ts:86 exports dispatch() — parse, claim idempotency, re-authorize at execution, optimistic concurrency — described in its own header as 'the one door business writes go through'. Grep across apps/web/src for `@/lib/commands` or `commands/bus` returns exactly zero importers, including tests: it is a door nobody uses, which makes WRK-050-002's execution, reauthorization and receipt steps declarations rather than behaviour. The other half is missing too: Bible §7.2's six risk classes (A0_OBSERVE..A5_PROTECTED_DOMAIN) appear nowhere in code, and §7.3's rule that 'the confirmation is bound to a digest of the exact plan' has no digest, no plan and no preview — grep for planDigest / riskClass / ActionPlan across apps and packages returns nothing. Compensation and reconciliation likewise. FAIL, and partly for an ownership reason that must not be worked around: dispatch() requires an idempotency store (CommandPorts.claimIdempotency at bus.ts:44-49) and apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma has no IdempotencyRecord model — the only idempotencyKey in the schema is ApprovalRequest's at :485. apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma is owned by another cluster run, and so is packages/contracts, where ToolRegistration would have to carry `riskClass`.
smallest_real_change: Ship the half that does not need another run's files, and record the rest as FAIL naming them. Implementable now: apps/web/src/lib/commands/action-plan.ts defines the six risk classes and planDigest(plan) — a canonical, key-order-independent SHA-256 over provider, acting identity, target, recipients, body, attachments, permission impact and notification flag (the same canonicalisation discipline apps/web/src/lib/provisioning/reconcile.ts:118-124 already documents for DynamoDB round-trips) — plus confirmationIsStillValid(approvedDigest, currentPlan) which refuses when any of those fields changed. Give it a real caller inside a file this run owns: apps/web/src/app/(app)/calendar/actions.ts creates events with attendee notification, so compute the digest at preview, carry it through the form, and re-derive and compare before the write, refusing when it moved. MUTATION PROOF: submit a confirmed plan whose recipient list was altered between preview and submit and assert the action refuses; then mutate the producer — drop `recipients` from the digest input in calendar/actions.ts — and that test must red. BLOCKED, and must not be edited by this run: routing any action through commands/bus.ts dispatch() needs an IdempotencyRecord model in apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma, and attaching riskClass to a tool needs ToolRegistration in packages/contracts. Both belong to another cluster run. WRK-050-002 therefore stays FAIL after this change, with those two files named.
